questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with a painless indurated ulcer on the glans penis for 2 weeks. Inguinal lymph nodes are enlarged but non-tender. Dark-field microscopy reveals motile spirochetes. Which of the following is the first-line treatment?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (Treponema pallidum) is treated with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM as a single dose. This remains the standard of care per WHO and IADVL guidelines.

questions.q: A 28-year-old HIV-positive man presents with multiple painless, flesh-coloured umbilicated nodules on the face and trunk. Histopathology shows cells with a large intracytoplasmic inclusion body (Henderson-Patterson body). What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum is caused by a poxvirus. Its hallmark histological feature is the Henderson-Patterson body (large intracytoplasmic viral inclusion). It is common and severe in immunocompromised patients.

questions.q: A 22-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus develops a tense bullous eruption on sun-exposed areas. Skin biopsy shows neutrophilic infiltrate at the dermal-epidermal junction. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgA deposits at the BMZ. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bullous SLE presents with tense bullae on sun-exposed skin in SLE patients. DIF shows linear or granular IgG, IgA, or IgM deposits. It responds dramatically to dapsone, distinguishing it from other bullous disorders.

questions.q: A 45-year-old agricultural worker from Bihar presents with progressive painless swelling of the foot with multiple discharging sinuses. The granules from the discharge are white. KOH mount shows hyaline septate hyphae. What is the most likely causative organism?
questions.exp: White grains in mycetoma with hyaline septate hyphae on KOH suggest eumycetoma caused by Scedosporium apiospermum (formerly Pseudallescheria boydii). Madurella gives black grains; Actinomadura madurae (white grains) is actinomycetoma (filamentous bacteria, not fungi).

questions.q: A 30-year-old man presents with hypopigmented anaesthetic patches on the trunk, thickened greater auricular nerve, and claw hand deformity. Slit-skin smear shows a bacteriological index (BI) of 3+. According to the Ridley-Jopling classification, where does this patient fall?
questions.exp: BI of 3+ with nerve thickening, anaesthetic patches, and claw hand deformity indicates multibacillary leprosy. The combination of features with a high BI places this in the BL (borderline lepromatous) spectrum on the Ridley-Jopling scale.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman on long-term hydroxychloroquine for discoid lupus develops decreased visual acuity. Fundoscopy shows a 'bull's eye' maculopathy. What is the mechanism of this drug toxicity?
opts: Accumulation in melanin-containing cells of the retinal pigment epithelium
Cataract formation due to oxidative stress
questions.exp: Hydroxychloroquine binds to melanin in the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), causing dose-dependent retinal toxicity. Bull's eye maculopathy results from progressive RPE damage. Annual ophthalmological screening is mandatory.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man presents with a raised, pearly, telangiectatic nodule on the nose that has bled twice. Dermoscopy shows arborizing vessels. What is the most appropriate treatment for this 8 mm lesion on the nasal tip?
opts: Standard surgical excision with 4 mm margins
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma on the nose (H-zone high-risk area) requires Mohs micrographic surgery for maximal margin control and tissue sparing. Mohs is preferred for BCCs on the face, recurrent lesions, and ill-defined borders.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman develops a diffuse morbilliform rash, fever, and facial oedema 3 weeks after starting carbamazepine for epilepsy. Labs show eosinophilia and elevated liver enzymes. What syndrome does this represent?
questions.exp: DRESS (Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms) classically occurs 2-8 weeks after drug initiation with aromatic anticonvulsants like carbamazepine. Features include fever, rash, eosinophilia, atypical lymphocytosis, and multi-organ involvement (liver commonest).

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with pain, tenderness, and erythema over the anterior shin bilaterally. The lesions are ill-defined, warm, and nodular. She was recently treated for streptococcal pharyngitis. Histology best confirms the diagnosis with which finding?
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum is the most common form of panniculitis. Histologically it shows septal panniculitis without vasculitis. Post-streptococcal trigger is classic. Granuloma formation at fibrous septa (Miescher's radial granulomas) is pathognomonic.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man presents with a slowly enlarging, waxy yellowish plaque on the medial canthus of both eyelids. Histology shows foamy macrophages and Touton giant cells in the dermis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Xanthelasma palpebrarum is characterised by yellowish periorbital plaques due to lipid-laden macrophages and Touton giant cells. It is associated with hyperlipidaemia in approximately 50% of cases.

questions.q: A 19-year-old presents with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base on the lips that recur every few weeks, preceded by tingling. Tzanck smear reveals multinucleated giant cells. Which antiviral regimen is recommended for long-term suppressive therapy?
opts: Acyclovir 200 mg five times daily for 5 days
questions.exp: For recurrent herpes labialis with frequent outbreaks (>6/year), suppressive therapy with valacyclovir 500 mg OD or acyclovir 400 mg BD is guideline-recommended. Valacyclovir offers the convenience of once-daily dosing.

questions.q: A 32-year-old man with psoriasis develops DIP joint swelling, nail pitting, and dactylitis ('sausage digit'). Which HLA type is most strongly associated with psoriatic arthritis with axial involvement?
questions.exp: Psoriatic arthritis with axial involvement (sacroiliitis, spondylitis) is strongly associated with HLA-B27. HLA-Cw6 is associated with plaque psoriasis vulgaris. HLA-DR4 is linked to rheumatoid arthritis.

questions.q: A 5-year-old child presents with circular areas of hair loss with broken hair stubs at the scalp margin. Wood's lamp examination shows bright green fluorescence. What is the most likely causative organism?
questions.exp: Microsporum canis causes tinea capitis (ectothrix infection) with bright green fluorescence on Wood's lamp due to pteridine production. Trichophyton tonsurans causes endothrix infection and does NOT fluoresce. Epidermophyton does not infect hair.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman on long-term systemic corticosteroids develops skin fragility, easy bruising, and atrophic scars. Which dermal cell type is primarily responsible for collagen synthesis in normal skin, and whose activity is suppressed by corticosteroids?
questions.exp: Fibroblasts synthesise Type I and Type III collagen, elastin, and glycosaminoglycans in the dermis. Long-term corticosteroid use suppresses fibroblast proliferation and collagen synthesis, causing skin atrophy, striae, and impaired wound healing.

questions.q: A 48-year-old man presents with intensely pruritic grouped vesicles and papules on the extensor elbows and buttocks. Biopsy shows neutrophilic microabscesses at dermal papillae tips. Direct immunofluorescence shows granular IgA deposits in dermal papillae. What is the most appropriate treatment?
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (Duhring's disease) shows granular IgA in dermal papillae and is associated with gluten-sensitive enteropathy (coeliac disease). Dapsone provides rapid relief of pruritus. Gluten-free diet is the definitive long-term treatment.

questions.q: A 70-year-old woman presents with tense bullae on the abdomen and flexures. Nikolsky's sign is negative. ELISA shows high titres of anti-BP180 (NC16A domain) antibodies. At which ultrastructural level is the primary cleavage in this condition?
opts: Within the epidermis at the desmosome level
Lamina lucida at the hemidesmosome-BMZ interface
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid targets BP180 (type XVII collagen) and BP230 at the hemidesmosome in the lamina lucida, producing sub-epidermal blisters. The tense blister and negative Nikolsky distinguish it from pemphigus (intra-epidermal, Nikolsky positive).

questions.q: A 16-year-old with moderate acne is started on oral isotretinoin 0.5 mg/kg/day. Which of the following is the primary mechanism by which isotretinoin achieves long-term remission?
opts: Reduction of sebaceous gland size and sebum production
Direct bactericidal activity against C. acnes
Blockade of androgen receptors in follicular epithelium
questions.exp: Isotretinoin (13-cis retinoic acid) causes involution (apoptosis) of sebaceous glands, reducing sebum by up to 90%. It also normalises follicular keratinisation and has anti-inflammatory effects. Sebaceous gland suppression accounts for its unique long-term remission.

questions.q: A 38-year-old man from Tamil Nadu presents with bilateral symmetric nodular infiltration of the face giving a 'leonine facies,' loss of eyebrows (madarosis), and nasal stuffiness. Slit-skin smear BI is 6+. What is the WHO recommended MDT regimen?
opts: Rifampicin 600 mg + Dapsone 100 mg daily for 6 months
Rifampicin 600 mg monthly + Clofazimine 300 mg monthly + Clofazimine 50 mg daily + Dapsone 100 mg daily for 12 months
Rifampicin 600 mg monthly + Dapsone 100 mg daily for 12 months
Rifampicin 600 mg + Clofazimine 50 mg + Dapsone 100 mg daily for 24 months
questions.exp: WHO MDT for multibacillary leprosy (PB = up to 5 patches; MB = >5 patches, any BI+) consists of monthly supervised rifampicin 600 mg + clofazimine 300 mg, plus daily clofazimine 50 mg + dapsone 100 mg for 12 months.

questions.q: A 25-year-old sexually active woman presents with multiple painful shallow vulval ulcers with a necrotic base and surrounding erythema. Gram stain shows coccobacilli in a 'school of fish' arrangement. Which organism is responsible?
questions.exp: Chancroid is caused by Haemophilus ducreyi. It presents with painful soft ulcers (unlike the painless ulcer of syphilis) and tender inguinal bubo ('school of fish' Gram stain). Treatment: azithromycin 1 g single dose or ceftriaxone 250 mg IM.

questions.q: A 45-year-old man with plaque psoriasis has extensive disease covering >20% BSA. He fails methotrexate and cyclosporine. Which biological drug specifically targets the IL-23/IL-17 axis by blocking the p19 subunit of IL-23?
questions.exp: Risankizumab is an anti-IL-23 biologic that selectively inhibits the p19 subunit of IL-23, blocking Th17 differentiation. Secukinumab and ixekizumab target IL-17A directly. Etanercept blocks TNF-alpha.

questions.q: A 60-year-old farmer presents with multiple firm subcutaneous nodules on the dorsum of the right hand and forearm, arranged linearly along lymphatics, following a thorn prick 3 months ago. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Sporotrichoid (lymphocutaneous) spread following thorn prick is the classic presentation of Sporothrix schenckii infection. The dimorphic fungus lives in soil and plant debris. Treatment: itraconazole 200 mg BD or saturated potassium iodide (SSKI).

questions.q: A 30-year-old presents with flesh-coloured verrucous perianal papules (condyloma acuminata). HPV DNA typing shows HPV 6 and 11. Which of the following vaccines targets these specific HPV types?
questions.exp: Both the quadrivalent (Gardasil) and nonavalent (Gardasil 9) vaccines cover HPV 6 and 11 (responsible for ~90% of genital warts). The bivalent vaccine targets only high-risk types 16 and 18. Post-treatment vaccination reduces recurrence.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman with Crohn's disease develops a rapidly enlarging, painful ulcer on the shin with a purulent base and undermined violaceous border. Pathergy test is positive. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Pyoderma gangrenosum is a neutrophilic dermatosis associated with IBD (Crohn's, UC), haematological malignancies, and arthritis. Classic features: painful ulcer with undermined violaceous edges, positive pathergy. Treatment: systemic corticosteroids or ciclosporin.

questions.q: During patch testing for allergic contact dermatitis, a positive reaction to nickel sulphate is read at 48 hours. Which type of hypersensitivity reaction underlies allergic contact dermatitis?
questions.exp: Allergic contact dermatitis is a classic Type IV (delayed-type) hypersensitivity mediated by sensitised CD4+ Th1 and CD8+ cytotoxic T cells, not antibodies. The reaction peaks at 48-96 hours after antigen re-exposure.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman with long-standing Raynaud's phenomenon and sclerodactyly has anti-centromere antibody positivity. Which life-threatening internal complication is she most at risk for compared to diffuse SSc?
questions.exp: Anti-centromere antibody is the hallmark of limited cutaneous SSc (lcSSc/CREST syndrome). The main visceral risk in lcSSc is pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Scleroderma renal crisis and extensive ILD are more characteristic of diffuse SSc (anti-SCL-70/Topo-I).

questions.q: A 3-year-old boy develops sudden generalised erythema and large sheet-like peeling of skin after an upper respiratory tract infection. He is afebrile and blood cultures are negative. Staphylococcus aureus is cultured from the nasopharynx. What toxin causes skin cleavage?
opts: Exfoliative toxin A or B (serine proteases)
questions.exp: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome (SSSS) is caused by exfoliative toxins A and B from phage group II S. aureus. These serine proteases cleave desmoglein-1 in the granular layer, causing intra-epidermal cleavage and sheet-like peeling.

questions.q: A 35-year-old HIV-positive man (CD4 = 80 cells/µL) develops dark violaceous plaques on the lower legs. Biopsy shows spindle cell proliferation with slit-like vascular spaces, extravasated red blood cells, and plasma cells. Which virus is implicated?
questions.exp: Kaposi's sarcoma is caused by HHV-8 (Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus / KSHV). It is an AIDS-defining illness. Histology: spindle cells, slit-like vascular channels, haemosiderin deposits. HAART is the cornerstone of management.

questions.q: During a patch test reading at 96 hours, an erythematous papular reaction without vesicles is observed at the test site. According to the ICDRG grading scale, this is classified as:
questions.exp: ICDRG grading: doubtful (?) = faint erythema only; weakly positive (+) = erythema, infiltration, possible papules; strongly positive (++) = erythema, papules, vesicles; extreme (+++) = coalescing vesicles. Papular reaction without vesicles = +.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman presents with recurrent episodes of intensely pruritic wheals and angioedema lasting less than 24 hours, recurring for over 6 weeks. All individual lesions resolve without post-inflammatory pigmentation. What is the first-line treatment?
questions.exp: Second-generation H1-antihistamines (cetirizine, levocetirizine, fexofenadine, loratadine) are first-line therapy for chronic spontaneous urticaria per EAACI and IADVL guidelines. If insufficient at licensed dose, up-dosing to 4x is recommended before adding omalizumab.

questions.q: A 28-year-old man with severe atopic dermatitis unresponsive to topical therapy is started on dupilumab. Which signalling pathway does dupilumab primarily block?
opts: IL-12/IL-23 pathway via the p40 subunit
IL-4 and IL-13 via the shared IL-4Ra receptor subunit
questions.exp: Dupilumab is a human monoclonal antibody targeting IL-4 receptor alpha (IL-4Ra), blocking signalling by both IL-4 and IL-13 — the central Th2 cytokines in atopic dermatitis. It is approved for moderate-to-severe AD in adults and children.

questions.q: A 50-year-old man presents with a gradually enlarging, well-demarcated erythematous plaque with central clearing on the medial thigh. The border is raised and scaly. KOH preparation shows septate hyphae. Treatment with terbinafine is planned. What is terbinafine's mechanism of action?
opts: Inhibition of 14-alpha demethylase (CYP51), blocking ergosterol synthesis
Inhibition of squalene epoxidase, causing squalene accumulation
Disruption of fungal cell membrane integrity
Inhibition of beta-glucan synthase, weakening the cell wall
questions.exp: Terbinafine inhibits squalene epoxidase, causing squalene accumulation within fungal cells. This is directly fungicidal for dermatophytes. In contrast, azoles (fluconazole, itraconazole) inhibit CYP51 (14-alpha demethylase). Echinocandins inhibit beta-glucan synthase.
